_comment: frank-exchange-of-views's own tool dependencies — aggregated by /prosthetic-conscience:doctor (each plugin owns its manifest; the doctor reports the whole suite). PLUGIN-SHIPPED BINARIES DO NOT BELONG HERE: this manifest lists EXTERNAL tools, checked by running them on PATH. A binary the plugin ships lives in its own bin/ and is discovered by sc-doctor's binary scan, which reports it and can fetch it; listing it here as well produced a check that could never pass (installed to <plugin>/bin, checked on PATH) and so a permanently DEGRADED verdict after a fully successful --fix.
_eventSchema_comment: The EVENT-SCHEMA EPOCH of the feov-record binary this plugin ships. It answers ONE question — does this binary write the event shape these prompts read — and it moves only when that shape changes incompatibly. It is deliberately NOT a version: a release number moves for reasons the schema does not care about, and comparing release numbers made this check track shipping instead of compatibility. `feov-record --schema` prints it; `setup` refuses to start a run when the binary's epoch differs from this one. There is no compatibility window and no delta list: equal runs, unequal refuses. It lives here rather than in .claude-plugin/plugin.json because that manifest has a fixed published schema and an unknown field there makes `claude plugin validate` warn on every run.

tools.name: node
tools.purpose: runs the debate engine (debate.js) and the zero-token simulator

tools.name: uv
tools.purpose: Python tool runner — uvx launches the arxiv-latex MCP server (FEOV document extraction)

tools.name: pdftotext
tools.purpose: extracts a PDF's TEXT LAYER for the research seats (poppler-utils). MEASURED 2026-08-23: absent, run A's red-lens-r1-L1 fell back to page-image renders and produced a 4.29 MB transcript, 3.61 MB of it base64 page images — 6x the next-largest seat, for ONE lens slice. Lossy PDF handling has ranked the #1 capability gap in run friction across prior runs; without this the fallback is silent and the cost lands as context, not as an error

tools.name: tesseract
tools.purpose: OCR for a PDF with no text layer — the other half of the same gap. The pdf-reader MCP server uses it only when MCP_PDF_OCR_PRESET=tesseract is set in the environment, so the BINARY being present is necessary and not sufficient; the variable is checked by feov-record setup, which is where a research run will notice

tools.name: buf
tools.purpose: convert a raw record shard line to JSON for inspection (`buf convert internal/record/recordpb/record.proto --type feov.record.v1.Event --from -#format=txtpb --to -#format=json`) — diagnostics only; nothing in the build or a run needs it, and `scripts/protogen` deliberately does not
